key_insight: The study shows that AI adoption in Nigerian healthcare depends not just on the technology, but on whether the workforce is aware, trained, and ready to use it. It highlights major gaps in preparedness and identifies barriers that must be addressed before clinical AI can scale safely and effectively.
problem_solved: It addresses the question of whether healthcare professionals in Nigeria are prepared for clinical AI adoption, and what barriers—such as limited training, low awareness, and infrastructure constraints—stand in the way.
method: Cross-sectional survey of 761 healthcare professionals across multiple disciplines and practice settings in Nigeria.
Measured awareness, attitudes, preparedness, and perceived barriers to AI adoption.
Analyzed workforce readiness to inform practical implementation needs in LMIC healthcare systems.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the paper emphasizes that model performance alone is not enough for real-world deployment. Successful healthcare AI requires user readiness, workflow fit, and targeted training, especially in resource-constrained settings.
visual_elements: A readiness dashboard showing awareness, attitude, preparedness, and barriers scores.
A workflow diagram illustrating the path from AI development to clinical adoption.
An icon-based barrier map highlighting training, infrastructure, policy, and trust issues.
A multi-group bar chart comparing responses across professional roles or practice settings.
paper_title: Prepared Or Unprepared? Evaluating Healthcare Workforce Readiness for Clinical Adoption of Artificial Intelligence in Nigeria
paper_authors: Abbas M. Rabiu, Abdulrazaq A. Zubair, Um-mulkhairi Ibrahim, Tolulope Olusuyi, Shaheeda Farouq
